text:
incident-bot: PAGER — canary failure for release 'release/2025-07-19a' on model 'rw-medium-v2' — anomalous outputs detected on /v1/generate (error-like tokens, garbled completions). Trigger: canary error rate 47% over 5m. Paging: @oncall-jamie @sasha (release owner)

sasha: oncall, do you have eyes? I'm seeing alerts from canary dashboards. Pausing further rollout traffic now (flipping feature flag). :warning:

jamie: seeing runtime logs from canary nodes. A bunch of requests failing in decode step. Suspect tokenizer mismatch between weight bundle and tokenizer package. Pulling tokenizer version and model hash.

nate: I grabbed the manifest and the artifact from the canary hosts. Weight bundle hash doesn't match the release manifest. Expected sha256: 0a3b9f4c... got sha256: d41f6e22...

aleks: that explains the garbled tokens — if the model weights don't match the tokenizer vocab mapping we get offset shifts. Quick check: tokenizer package in image: tokenizer_v2025-07-01, release manifest expects tokenizer_v2025-07-19.

sasha: ugh. Where could the mismatch happen? CI artifact promotion?

nate: logs from the promotion job show a successful upload but the tag applied was `rw-medium-v2:canary-latest` which aliased to an older weightset due to a concurrent promote. snippet from deploy pipeline: ```sh
# promotion step
gsutil cp weights/release-20250719/weights.tar.gz gs://releases/rw-medium-v2/weights-latest.tar.gz
# race window: another job overwrote weights-latest with 20250701 pack
```

jamie: immediate action: 1) flip kill flag to block traffic to canary variant 2) roll back canary routing to previous stable model 3) notify support/CS. I'm running kill flag now.

sasha: I flipped feature flag `model_rollout_rw_medium_v2` -> OFF and removed canary routing. Confirming new requests are routed to rw-medium-v1. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: ACTION: feature flag flip recorded by sasha at 1752102540. Canary traffic drained.

mia: support here. Customer impact: telemetry shows ~1200 requests returned garbled tokens in the 15 minutes during the canary window; ~8 customers had degraded outputs in evaluation. No data exposure, not authentication-related. I'm drafting a cautious customer note and triaging externally facing jobs.

aleks: recommended mitigation: pin model manifest hashes in release pipeline and add a guard that prevents promoting weights with mismatched tokenizer tags. Also add a post-promote validation step that runs a tiny tokenization + decode sanity test. Example quick check: ```py
# sanity test
input = "Hello world"
expected_tokens_prefix = [154, 24]  # release-known prefix
if model.tokenize(input)[:2] != expected_tokens_prefix:
    fail_promotion()
```

nate: rolling back the artifact tag to stable and re-promoting correct weights now. Starting rollforward safe path is blocked until CI validation added. ETA for stable routing: ~5m.

deploy-bot: ROLLBACK: routing switched to rw-medium-v1 at 1752102660. Health checks green.

jamie: monitoring for residual errors. Running through logs for any cache/kv mismatches. Also evacuating any worker nodes that pulled the bad weightset to force re-pull.

sasha: assigning postmortem and action items: - CI promote guard (nate) - post-promote tokenization check (aleks) - customer comms and incident summary (mia) - release playbook update for concurrent promotions (sasha)

mia: sent initial customer note to the 8 affected accounts and created follow-up tickets. No escalations so far.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: canary is aborted and traffic is on stable model. Observed error spike subsided to baseline within 3m of rollback. Severity downgraded.

jamie: final check: no ongoing pager alerts. I'll keep a high watch for 1h. If nothing else, close after RCA scheduled.

sasha: thanks team. We'll regroup in postmortem. :coffee:
